dedupe_keys.name: resilience of 45 urban metro rail networks worldwide under failure and recovery scenarios

description: This study in npj Sustainable Mobility and Transport (April 2026), by authors from Northeastern University, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and UC Berkeley, simulates seven failure and recovery scenarios on 45 urban metro rail networks around the world to examine how network topology shapes resilience. Metro systems are lifelines for mobility, access and economic activity but face natural and human-induced disruptions, and earlier work rarely combined varied failure and recovery strategies with topology across many systems. Analysing 25 network attributes, their interactions and collective behaviour, the authors find that a consistent group of attributes capturing connectivity, redundancy, loop structure and modular organisation is key to spotting structural vulnerabilities and improving resilience, with implications for design, retrofitting, emergency management and planning. A proof-of-concept retrofitting experiment shows targeted topological changes can improve failure resilience and speed recovery. Coverage: 45 metro networks. Access: open article. Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND, free. Caveats: topology-only models without passenger flows or hazard maps. It informs resilience, cascading failure and recovery planning of rail transit. It relates to the public transport networks of 25 cities and OSMnx in the catalogue.
